children: South Korea's strong semiconductor-led exports have prompted Barclays to raise its current account surplus forecasts for the coming years. Barclays now expects South Korea's current account surplus to come in at $440 billion in 2026 and $400 billion in 2027, up from its earlier estimates of $345 billion and $378.5 billion, respectively. Barclays economist Bum Ki Son says most of the surplus is driven by a goods-trade surplus owing to steady chip-led export momentum. South Korea's exports have already topped the full-year 2025 total by early September, according to customs data last week. (kwanwoo.jun@wsj.com)
